author: Claude Opus 5.5, 2026-11-21
notes: Counterfactual pairs: change one thing about a golden scenario and check the probability of the measured move(s) moves the expected way by at least minDelta (default 0.03). These isolate whether the model reads each part of the state.

pairs.title: Saver to spender: buying a car becomes more likely
pairs.rationale: Same money, a spender is far more likely to buy the car.

pairs.title: Index investor to stock picker: individual stocks up
Saver to real estate investor: rental up
Saver to entrepreneur: starting a business up
Spender to early retiree: index investing up
Only the persona text changes (balanced traits kept): car up
pairs.rationale: Tests whether the persona sentence alone moves the model.

pairs.title: Only the status trait changes (persona kept): big home or car up
pairs.rationale: Tests whether the traits line alone moves the model.

pairs.title: Mortgage rates 6.2% to 8.5%: rental down
pairs.rationale: Higher rates make leveraged rentals less attractive even for an investor.

pairs.title: Normal month to crash: big purchases down
pairs.rationale: A crash and a weak jobs report make people cautious.

pairs.title: Status seeker sees weak jobs and a falling market: car down
pairs.rationale: Even status seekers hesitate when the economy looks shaky.

pairs.title: Market up 6% in a boom: individual stocks up for a balanced planner
pairs.rationale: Ordinary people chase hot markets a little.

pairs.title: Stock picker who just lost $20k on stocks: stocks down

sim.memory: Sold the rest of the stocks at a loss

pairs.rationale: A fresh loss tempers even a confident trader.

pairs.title: Entrepreneur whose last business just failed: new business down
pairs.rationale: A fresh failure makes the next swing less likely.

pairs.title: Balanced planner just got a raise: home or investing up
pairs.rationale: Good news makes the natural next step (home, investing) more likely.

pairs.title: Add $12k of 24% card debt: investing down
pairs.rationale: With expensive debt, paying it off should take money away from investing.

pairs.title: Employed to laid off for four months: holding cash up
pairs.rationale: Without a paycheck, holding cash is the natural response.

pairs.title: Town rentals 2 of 20 empty to 18 of 40: rental down
pairs.rationale: Lots of empty rentals in town is a warning sign for another one.

pairs.title: Teacher 62 to 66: retiring more likely
pairs.rationale: Closer to the usual retirement age, retiring becomes more likely.
